turns.content: hey, so i just checked the guild charter again and section 4 says "anyone who attends at least five sanctioned weekend sessions within a rolling eight-week window qualifies as an active member" — i have my attendance noted: june 1st, 8th, 15th, 22nd, and 29th. that's five straight weekends. does that mean i meet the written criteria? i'm not trying to jump the line or anything, it's just... showing up five weekends in a row took a lot of planning for me, so i'd like to know where i stand. 🤔

On the text you quoted, the arithmetic works: five sessions between June 1 and June 29 span 28 days, inside an 8-week (56-day) window. Whether you meet the criteria depends on three things the quote doesn't settle.

**1. The dates don't fall on a weekend in 2026.** June 1, 8, 15, 22, and 29, 2026 are all Mondays. In 2025 they were all Sundays. So either:
- the sessions were in June 2025 — in which case they were weekend sessions, but the 8-week rolling window containing them closed around July 27, 2025, and "rolling" ordinarily means the window is measured from today backward; or
- the sessions were in June 2026 — in which case they weren't weekend sessions as the charter defines them, unless the guild treats Monday sessions as "weekend" or you've recorded the dates one day off.

Check the year and the actual calendar dates against the guild's own session list before asserting the count.

**2. "Sanctioned."** Each of the five must be a session the guild officially designated. Your attendance note doesn't establish that; the guild's session calendar or officer records would.

**3. Whose record counts.** You said your attendance is "noted." If that means your notes, the guild may only recognize its own sign-in or roster. If it means the guild's records, that point is closed.

**Bottom line:** if the five sessions were guild-sanctioned weekend sessions recorded by the guild and fall within the last 56 days, the quoted text is satisfied. Given the calendar problem above, at least one of those conditions is currently in doubt.

**Next step:** ask whoever maintains attendance (an officer or secretary) for the guild's record of your five dates and confirm the year and day of week. If the sessions were in 2025, ask how the charter treats status after a qualifying window ends — some charters make it persistent, some require re-qualification; Section 4 as quoted doesn't say.

oh wait, that's a good point about the days... i just looked back at my calendar and they're actually saturdays in 2025 — june 1 was a sunday actually, i wrote it down wrong. so june 7th, 14th, 21st, 28th, and july 5th? no, july 5th is a saturday too. let me check my notes... yeah, five saturdays in a row. does that fix the calendar problem?

Partly. The corrected dates are all Saturdays: June 7, 14, 21, 28, and July 5, 2025 (June 1, 2025 was a Sunday, so June 7 was a Saturday). Span is 28 days, within 56. That resolves the day-of-week issue.

Two things remain open.

**1. The year.** Today is September 11, 2026. An 8-week window measured back from today covers July 17–September 11, 2026. Sessions in June–July 2025 are roughly 14 months outside it. Whether they still count depends on how the guild reads "rolling":
- If "rolling" means the window is assessed as of now, you don't currently qualify on those five dates.
- If the charter means that satisfying the criterion in *any* 8-week window confers status that then persists, you qualified as of July 5, 2025, and the question is whether anything since has revoked it. Section 4 as quoted doesn't address persistence or lapse.

**2. The reliability of the dates.** They've changed twice in this conversation (Mondays 2026 → Saturdays starting June 1 → Saturdays starting June 7). That's normal for reconstructing from memory, but it means your notes shouldn't be the basis for a formal claim. The guild's sign-in or roster is what would settle it, and it may also settle whether each session was "sanctioned."

**Bottom line:** if the guild's records show those five Saturdays, the five-in-eight-weeks arithmetic is satisfied for the window ending July 5, 2025. Whether that translates to active status *today* is unresolved by the text you've quoted.

**Next step:** ask the officer who keeps attendance for (a) the guild's record of your 2025 sessions and (b) how the guild applies "rolling" — as of today, or as of any qualifying window. If there's a lapse clause elsewhere in the charter, that's the section to read.

hmm that's... a lot to think about. i guess i didn't consider the year gap. so if the rolling window means "right now," those dates are way too old. that's a bit disappointing but makes sense.

the charter doesn't mention anything about persistence or lapse — just the five weekends thing. so maybe i'm overthinking it and i should just ask julian next saturday? 🤷

Asking Julian is the right next step, and it doesn't require more analysis from you first.

Two points before you do.

**Silence in the charter cuts both ways.** If Section 4 says nothing about persistence or lapse, the text alone doesn't tell you whether status expires. That's an interpretive question the guild has presumably had to answer for other members before. Julian (or whoever administers membership) either knows the working practice or will need to decide it — either way, that's information you can't get from re-reading the clause.

**What to ask, specifically:**
1. What do the guild's own records show for your attendance in June–July 2025?
2. Does the guild read "rolling eight-week window" as measured from the present, or as "any eight-week window in which the criterion was met"?
3. If the latter, has anyone previously been treated as lapsed, and on what basis?

Asking (1) first matters: if the guild's records don't show five sessions, questions (2) and (3) are moot.

**If the answer is "measured from the present":** you'd need five sanctioned weekend sessions within any 56-day span going forward. Starting next Saturday (September 19, 2026), the earliest completion date with consecutive weekends is October 17, 2026 — well inside the window. That's the same effort as last year, but this time you'd know the record is the guild's, not yours.

Bring your reconstructed dates (June 7, 14, 21, 28, July 5, 2025) as a reference for Julian to check against, not as the claim itself.

yeah, i think asking julian is the move. i'll take my notes just in case he wants to check. honestly, even if the answer is no, it was still nice to push myself to show up that many times. i used to bail on things after two weeks.

Bringing the notes as a reference for Julian to check against is the right use of them.

On the last point: what you've reported is five consecutive Saturdays (June 7–July 5, 2025) against a prior pattern of stopping after roughly two weeks. That's an observable change in one instance; whether it holds is something you'd learn from the next stretch, and the guild's roster would document it either way.

If Julian says the window is measured from the present, five sanctioned Saturdays starting September 19, 2026 would complete by October 17 — the same commitment, with the guild's record rather than yours as the basis.
yeah you're right, the guild record is the thing that matters. i'll just ask him straight up. thanks for talking it through, it helped me get my head straight before saturday.

That's the plan: ask Julian for the guild's record of your June–July 2025 attendance and how "rolling" is applied, with your dates (June 7, 14, 21, 28, July 5, 2025) as a cross-check.
